name: Haneda-Airport-Terminal-1-2
tagline: Shinagawa in 37 minutes and Tokyo in 43 minutes. Served by 2 lines.
summary: The station is in Ota City, where Keikyu and Tokyo Monorail run 2 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 48 minutes to Otemachi, 57 minutes to Shinjuku, 52 minutes to Shibuya and 37 minutes to Shinagawa. The station stands 3.1 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 2.5 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 3.1 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 3.1 m to 5.6 m, a difference of 2.5 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, neither the station nor any of the nine points within 400 m of it falls inside the projected inundation area. On the whole, the flood projection here is among the smallest in the 23 wards.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station: Keikyu Airport Line and Tokyo Monorail. The lines are split between operators (Keikyu runs 1 line and Tokyo Monorail runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: The ministry's congestion survey does not publish figures for Keikyu Airport Line and Tokyo Monorail. It covers the major commuter stretches, and this line is not among them.

neighbours.lead: Shin-Seibijo is ahead on quiet, but Haneda-Airport-Terminal-1-2 is ahead on the number of lines.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Haneda-Airport-Terminal-1-2. Shin-Seibijo has only the Tokyo Monorail, so Haneda-Airport-Terminal-1-2 is the better connected. To Shinagawa, for instance, Shin-Seibijo takes 4 minutes longer. On quiet, though, Shin-Seibijo comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: Haneda-Airport-Terminal-3 is ahead on quiet, but Haneda-Airport-Terminal-1-2 is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection.
neighbours.note: About 1.5 km from Haneda-Airport-Terminal-1-2 in a straight line. It is served by the same lines as Haneda-Airport-Terminal-1-2. To Toranomon, for instance, Haneda-Airport-Terminal-3 is 5 minutes quicker. On quiet, Haneda-Airport-Terminal-3 comes out ahead.

noiseSources: The 首都高速湾岸線 viaduct runs right beside the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
東京湾岸道路 (3 lanes each way) runs right beside the station. Traffic on it never stops, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: OpenStreetMap records no supermarket within walking distance of the station.
leads.hazards: Neither the station nor the ground around it falls inside the projected flood area.
leads.stationNote: 2 lines serve the station. The choice of connections is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is low for the 23 wards.
leads.noiseSources: At this station, check the traffic noise before the noise people make.
